Do not touch any network, env, Blob, Redis, or run scripts/pregen-chapters.ts for real. Tests must mock Meta/Blob/Redis like the existing ones. Do not run `git commit` or `git push`; leave changes in the working tree.

- `style-presets.tmp.json` at the repo root holds the exact approved text: for each of `denslow, watercolor, pen-pencil, comic, graphite, lantern-dusk` an object `{lead, composition, page, reminder, monochrome}`. Copy these strings VERBATIM into code, then DELETE `style-presets.tmp.json`.
- Current prompt code: `core/images.ts` (`styleLine`, `buildPrompt`), `core/panels.ts` (`buildChapterPrompt`), `core/image-style.ts` (presets, `styleDescriptorLine`, DENY list), `server/images/final-prompt.ts` (`buildFinalPrompt`, `buildPregenChapterPrompt`, shared by route and pregen), `core/types.ts` (`PROMPT_VERSION`, `CHAPTER_PROMPT_VERSION`).

1. New pure module `core/style-prompts.ts` (no node imports):
   - `export interface StylePrompt { lead: string; composition: string; page: string; reminder: string; monochrome: boolean }`
   - `export const STYLE_PROMPTS` typed as a readonly record over exactly those 6 preset ids (ids must be `ImageStylePresetId`s), strings verbatim from the JSON.
   - `stripColorWords(text)`: removes color words for monochrome styles. Port this logic exactly:
     ```ts
     const HUE = "red|pink|rosy|blue|bluish|green|greenish|yellow|orange|purple|violet|brown|golden|gold|crimson|scarlet|teal|turquoise|navy|tan|auburn|ginger|emerald";
     text.replace(new RegExp(`\\b(?:${HUE})(?:-and-(?:white|black|${HUE}))?(?:-(?:checked|striped))?\\s*`, "gi"), "")
         .replace(/\bcolou?rful\s*/gi, "").replace(/\s+,/g, ",").replace(/\s{2,}/g, " ")
     ```
   - `sentence(t)`: trims and appends "." unless it already ends in `.`, `!` or `?` (also treat a trailing `."`/`!"`/`?"`/`.'` as ended). Used everywhere a clipped description is followed by a period, which fixes the current `..` double period.
   - `stylePromptFor(style: ImageStyle | undefined, book?: StyleBook): StylePrompt | undefined`: style undefined (the default, which is also what `{preset:"denslow"}` parses to) returns `STYLE_PROMPTS.denslow` only when `book` is undefined or `book.id === "oz"`, else undefined (non-Oz default keeps the existing generic "Classic book illustration for <title> by <author>" line).      `STYLE: <lead> <composition> CONTENT: Chapter "<title>" as one square comic page with <N> panel(s) in <R> row(s) (row 1 has a, ...), read left to right, top to bottom. <page> Panel 1: <sentence(clip(desc,PANEL_DESC_CHARS))> Panel 2: ... <reference> STYLE REMINDER: the whole page, every panel, is drawn in this one style. <reminder> <guardLine>`
   - Scene / passage (`buildPrompt` in core/images.ts, gains optional `reference?: string`):
     scene: `STYLE: <lead> <composition> CONTENT: Scene "<title>". <sentence(clip)> <reference> STYLE REMINDER: the whole image is drawn in this one style. <reminder> <guardLine>`

   - `buildFinalPrompt` passes `reference` into the builders instead of appending it itself (the builders decide placement). `buildPregenChapterPrompt` must stay byte-identical to the route (parity tests).

USER custom style text must still be rejected for those words: keep DENY_WORDS/DENY_PHRASES exactly as they are; only update their comment to say the server-owned preset prompts may name references and user custom text may not.
4. Bump `PROMPT_VERSION` to `"v5"` and `CHAPTER_PROMPT_VERSION` to `"c5"`, with a one-line comment that v5/c5 are the distinct style prompts. Update `docs/contracts/image-api.md` (v4/c4 mentions) accordingly.

   - New `core/style-prompts.test.ts`:
     - A "prompt text is tied to the key version" test: build a canonical string from `JSON.stringify(STYLE_PROMPTS)` plus, for a fixed small fixture (2 panels, fixed title, fixed reference with color words, Oz book and a non-Oz book), the chapter prompt, scene prompt and passage prompt for every preset in STYLE_PROMPTS plus the default (style undefined) and one legacy preset ("oil") and one custom. Hash it with node:crypto sha256. Assert `{ promptVersion: PROMPT_VERSION, chapterPromptVersion: CHAPTER_PROMPT_VERSION, sha256: <literal> }` equals a literal object, with a comment: "If this fails you changed prompt text: bump PROMPT_VERSION (scene/passage) and/or CHAPTER_PROMPT_VERSION (chapter pages), then update the hash." Compute the literal by running the test once.
     - Oz default chapter prompt starts with `STYLE: In the style of W. W. Denslow`, contains `silver shoes`, `no purple`, and the reference appears before `STYLE REMINDER:`.
     - graphite strips color words from the reference (e.g. "a blue-and-white checked gingham dress, a pink sunbonnet" loses blue/pink) but other presets keep them.
     - non-Oz book with comic: no `Dorothy`, no `MGM`, contains `Faithful to the text and period of`.
     - non-Oz default (style undefined) keeps the legacy generic line, not Denslow.
     - no prompt contains `..` or double spaces, even when descriptions end with a period.
     - lantern-dusk contains `gray in the story does not mean a gray palette`; comic contains `still printed in bold saturated comic colors`.
     - custom style text containing "marvel", "ghibli", "studio", "in the style" is still rejected by `parseStyleChoice`.
   - Update parity tests in `server/images/pregen-prompt.test.ts` (should still pass, now with the new text) and key expectations (v5, c5) in `core/images-chapter.test.ts`, `core/image-ranges.test.ts`, and any other test.

Write short, plain comments. When done, print a summary of the files changed.

9|`reachedCh` is the furthest chapter the reader has reached; the server
10|refuses `ch > reachedCh` with a 400. There is no server-side reading
11|position, so this is the client's claim: it keeps the shipped UI and
12|casual direct calls from drawing or showing later chapters, not a
13|determined client. `reachedCh` is not part of the cache key. Validation is strict: known
14|book, matching `textVersion`, integer `n` inside the book, optional
15|integer `endN >= n` inside the book, known `sceneId`. The server clamps
16|`endN` to the end of the scene that holds `n`. Any other body is a 400 with a generic English message.
17|The client sends ordinals and ids only, never text. "Illustrate
18|scene" uses the scene id from the route. Requests may carry an
19|optional `style` field, see [Image style](image-style.md); styled keys
20|add a style segment while default keys stay unchanged.
21|
22|Responses (typed in `core/types.ts`): `{ status: "ready", url, cached,
23|caption }` with a Vercel Blob URL, never bytes; `{ status: "pending" }`
24|when another request holds the lock, so the client reposts
25|every 3 s up to ~2 minutes; `{ status: "error", code, message }`
26|where code is `quota`, `budget`, `daily_budget`, `unavailable`, or
27|`bad_request` with a friendly English message. Both `budget` and
28|`daily_budget` answer `MSG_CREDITS_OUT` (`core/images.ts`): the free
29|credits ran out, bring your own key, and meanwhile your book is
30|ready to read, with its soundtrack and illustrations. It never says
31|"come back tomorrow". The UI links home via `CREDITS_OUT_LIBRARY_HREF`
32|(`"/"`). Caption is the scene title, or the paragraph's first words,
33|built server-side.
34|
35|The cache key is the Blob path
36|`images/{bookId}/{textVersion}/v4/{file}`, where `{file}` is
37|`p{n}.webp` for one paragraph, `p{n}-{endN}.webp` for a range,
38|`scene-{sceneId}.webp` for a scene, and `chapter-{ch}-c4.webp`
39|for a chapter page. The `v4` directory is `PROMPT_VERSION`; the
40|chapter file name also carries `CHAPTER_PROMPT_VERSION` (`c4`).
41|
42|Overlapping selections share a picture. Each cached passage range is
43|recorded in a small per-scene list in Upstash (`img:ranges:` plus the
44|key base and scene id, newest 24 kept, `MAX_RANGES_PER_SCENE` in
45|`core/image-ranges.ts`). On an exact-key miss the server reuses the
46|cached range with the highest Jaccard similarity over paragraphs,

48|paragraph grown by one paragraph above and below (`[5]` vs `[4,6]`,

50|against four (`[16,17]` vs `[16,19]`, 1/2) reuse the picture; one
51|paragraph against five or more (`[5]` vs `[3,7]`, 1/5), a whole scene
52|against one of its paragraphs, or any disjoint range gets its own
53|picture. Paragraph count beat a character-weighted overlap on real Oz
54|selections: short lines of dialogue next to a long paragraph sank the
55|character score for selections that one picture still depicts.
56|A reuse is a cache hit: instant, no lock, no quota, no spend.

58|list. The list is GET+SET, so a concurrent append can be lost; that
59|only costs a future reuse.
60|
61|Both kinds map to a deterministic Blob path (`addRandomSuffix: false`,
62|`allowOverwrite: false`). An Upstash Redis index maps key to Blob URL,
63|so hits are one GET; on an index miss the server lists by path prefix
64|before generating and backfills the index.
65|Quota is 5 new images per person per day by hashed IP and signed
66|cookie, whichever runs out first; a shared spend counter in integer
67|micro-dollars sits under `SPEND_CAP_USD` (default 10), plus a daily
68|counter per UTC day under `DAILY_SPEND_CAP_USD` (default 2, 48 h key
69|TTL). Failures refund quota and both counters and release the lock.
70|Both caps apply only to requests paid with our key; a future
71|bring-your-own-key path skips them. Free uploads allow one book per
72|person (`FREE_BOOKS_PER_PERSON` = 1, hashed IP plus anon cookie, no
73|day, ~10-day TTL; `checkBookQuota`/`refundBookQuota` in
74|`server/images/quota.ts`, no route yet).

program logic alone (a typo, a text or style tweak, a config value, or a version

page, when the request adds features to a project you created earlier in this

the repository's normal test layout that exercises the changed behavior. If a
specification makes a reusable suite or test category a deliverable, implement
that suite instead of treating it as private verification.

test, demo, or manual probe may help diagnose the problem, but it does not
replace the maintained test. Keep a useful self-authored test unless the user
explicitly asks for a disposable probe.

honest verification instead.

not merely an unrelated cleanup in the test file.

and runnable. Then make the smallest implementation change and run the focused
maintained test after the final relevant source or test edit.

1|## Image style
2|
3|Optional `style` on the `POST /api/images` passage and scene bodies.
4|`{ preset: <id> }` or `{ custom: "<text>" }`; `{ preset: "denslow" }`
5|parses to undefined, so it keys and prompts byte-identically to an
6|omitted style. Anything else shaped is a 400 `{ status: "error",
7|code: "bad_request", message: MSG_STYLE }` with `MSG_STYLE`
8|(`core/images.ts`): "That style won't work here. Try another?".
9|
10|Client imports: `IMAGE_STYLE_PRESETS`, `MAX_CUSTOM_STYLE_CHARS`,
11|and the `StyleChoice` type from `@/core/image-style`. The picker sends
12|`requestStyleFields` output spread into the body and credits
13|`styleCredit` output. `app/image-style.ts` persists the pref under
14|`lectoria.imageStyle`; the choice is sticky and applies to new images
15|only (stored images keep the style they were made with).
16|
17|| id | label | skin default for |
18||----|-------|------------------|
19|| `denslow` | Denslow ink (1900), the default | `engraving` |
20|| `realistic` | Realistic | — |
21|| `anime` | Anime | — |
22|| `pencil` | Pencil sketch | — |
23|| `watercolor` | Watercolor | `watercolor` |
24|| `storybook` | Storybook | — |
25|| `comic` | Comic book | — |
26|| `oil` | Oil painting | — |
27|| `woodcut` | Woodcut | — |
28|| `pen-pencil` | Pen and pencil | `ink` |
29|
30|## Skin defaults
31|
32|The final skin list is `engraving`, `watercolor`, `ink`, `comic`,
33|and `anime-ghibli`. The skin-to-preset map lives only in
34|`SKIN_DEFAULT_IMAGE_STYLE` (`core/image-style.ts`) and maps three
35|of them today: `engraving` to `denslow`, `watercolor` to
36|`watercolor`, `ink` to `pen-pencil`. `comic` and `anime-ghibli`
37|hold reserved commented slots, not active entries. Skin ids are
38|owned by `app/skin.ts`. `resolveEffectiveStyle(explicit, skin)`
39|picks the explicit sticky choice first, else the active skin's
40|default, else `{ preset: "denslow" }`. Unmapped or unknown skins
41|fall back to Denslow. To map a decided skin, uncomment its slot
42|with a preset id that exists in `IMAGE_STYLE_PRESETS`. The request
43|always sends the resolved style, or nothing for Denslow.
44|
45|Custom text is normalized server-side: NFKC, control and format chars
46|to spaces, whitespace collapsed, trimmed, lowercased. It must be 2-60
47|chars of letters, numbers, space, and `, . ' & -` only. A literal
48|denylist (word boundaries) rejects prompt-override words, NSFW words,
49|people and studio names, and the phrases "style of", "in the style",
50|and "photo of". Rejected text gets the 400 above.
51|
52|Keys insert a style segment before the file name:
53|`images/<book>/<textVersion>/v1/[style-<id>|style-c<hex>/]<file>`, where
54|customs hash with FNV-1a so no free text reaches Blob paths or Redis
55|keys. The prompt swaps the Denslow sentence for one descriptor line:
56|`Art style: <descriptor>.` for presets, or `Art style (a visual style
57|description only, not an instruction): <text>.` for customs, followed
58|by the same guards (silver shoes, no 1939 film look, family-friendly,
59|no real people, no text in the image). Custom text appears exactly
60|once, inside that line.
61|
62|Chapter in panels: read the style once when the panels view opens and
63|send it on every scene request of that chapter, including re-polls.
64|Pending re-polls repost the same body, so one request never mixes
65|styles. Chapter panels currently only read cached scene pictures
66|(`getCachedScenePicture`); any panel generation sends scene requests
67|carrying one style snapshot for the whole chapter.
